1: Runaways by Brian K. Vaughan (Marvel) is a superhero drama about teenagers who learn the worst possible thing about their families. Six kids who barely know each other are stuck together during their parents' yearly get-together, until they spy on the grown-ups and discover they are a secret society of supervillains. Horrified, the kids run away and set out to stop them. It is sharp, funny, and full of heart, a good pick for readers who like found-family stories.
2: Chibi Vampire is the light novel companion to Yuna Kagesaki's manga (Tokyopop), a gentle supernatural comedy and romance. Karin Maaka comes from a family of vampires, but she is the odd one out: instead of needing blood, she makes too much of it and has to give it back to people. Things get complicated around her classmate Kenta Usui, whose bad luck makes her blood surge. It is light, sweet, and a nice extra helping for fans of the manga.
3: Torture Princess: Fremd Torturchen by Keishi Ayasato (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy with a gothic, sharp-tongued edge. After a miserable life ends in murder, Kaito Sena is summoned to another world by Elisabeth Le Fanu, the Torture Princess, who wants him as her servant. Elisabeth has been ordered to hunt down demons and their contractors, and once she finishes, she herself is to be executed. It suits readers who like grim fantasy with a strange, tender core.
4: The Betrayal Knows My Name by Hotaru Odagiri (Yen Press) is a supernatural drama about fate, loyalty, and lives that echo across centuries. Yuki Sakurai is a kind orphan who can feel other people's pain through touch. When a mysterious man named Luka appears and swears to protect him, Yuki is drawn into an ancient war between the Giou clan and the demonic Duras. Fans of moody, beautifully drawn shojo fantasy will feel right at home.
5: Hana-Kimi: For You in Full Blossom by Hisaya Nakajo (Viz Media) is a cross-dressing school comedy and romance. Mizuki Ashiya, a girl living in America, is so inspired by high jumper Izumi Sano that she moves to Japan, cuts her hair, and enrolls at his all-boys high school. Sano has given up jumping, and Mizuki is determined to help him get back to it while keeping her secret. It is goofy, warm, and packed with a lovable cast of classmates.
6: Happy Kanako's Killer Life by Toshiya Wakabayashi (Seven Seas) is an action comedy about finding the right job in the wrong line of work. Kanako is an office worker worn down by a terrible boss and a job that makes her miserable. When she quits, she stumbles into work at an assassination company, and it turns out she is surprisingly good at it. It is bright, offbeat fun for readers who like their workplace comedies with a body count.
7: Hazure Skill: The Guild Member with a Worthless Skill Is Actually a Legendary Assassin by Kennoji (Yen Press) is a fantasy action comedy. Roland was the most feared assassin around, but he has retired and wants nothing more than a quiet desk job at the adventurers' guild. His old skills keep getting him noticed anyway, no matter how hard he tries to blend in. It is easygoing fantasy fun for fans of overpowered heroes trying to live an ordinary life.
8: The Girl I Saved on the Train Turned Out to Be My Childhood Friend by Kennoji (Yen Press) is a sweet school romantic comedy. On his morning train, Ryou Takamori steps in to help a girl being harassed, then slips away without a fuss. The girl turns out to be Hina Fushimi, his childhood friend, now the most popular girl at school, and she has not forgotten him. It is a light, gentle read for fans of slow-burn high school romance.
10: Heaven Official's Blessing by Mo Xiang Tong Xiu (Seven Seas) is a sweeping fantasy romance from China, full of gods, ghosts, and old legends. Xie Lian was once a beloved crown prince who rose to heaven, but he has been banished twice and is now a laughingstock among the gods. On his third ascension, he is sent on a mission and crosses paths with a mysterious young man, who may be the most feared ghost king of all. It is rich, funny, and deeply romantic.
12: The Hero Is Overpowered but Overly Cautious by Light Tuchihi (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy that pokes fun at the usual isekai hero. The goddess Ristarte needs a champion for a world that is extremely hard to save, so she summons Seiya Ryuuguuin, who has incredible stats. The catch is that Seiya is cautious to an absurd degree, training endlessly and preparing for every possible danger before taking a single step. It is a great pick for anyone who likes genre parody.
15: High-Rise Invasion by Tsuina Miura and Takahiro Oba (Seven Seas) is a tense action horror story. High school student Yuri Honjo suddenly finds herself on the roof of a skyscraper in a strange world of towers linked by rope bridges, where masked killers hunt anyone they find. Desperate to survive, she sets out to find her brother, who she hopes is somewhere in this world too. It moves fast and suits readers who like survival thrillers.
16: The Invisible Man and His Soon-to-Be Wife by Iwatobineko (Seven Seas) is a gentle mystery romance. A private detective who happens to be invisible takes on a new assistant, a young woman who is blind. Since neither can see the other, they get to know each other in their own way while they work through cases together. It is a quiet, cozy read for fans of tender romance with a touch of mystery.
18: The Maid I Hired Recently Is Mysterious by Wakame Konbu (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy with a small mystery at its heart. Yuuri is a young boy living alone in his big family home after losing his parents. He takes in a live-in maid named Lilith, who is kind, capable, and clearly hiding something. Their days together are full of teasing and sweetness, and it is a nice pick for readers who like gentle, warm romance.
19: O Maidens in Your Savage Season by Mari Okada and Nao Emoto (Kodansha) is a coming-of-age comedy and drama. Five girls in a high school literature club spend their days reading classic novels, until a club discussion turns to sex and suddenly no one can stop thinking about it. Each girl stumbles through crushes, embarrassment, and growing up in her own way. It is frank, funny, and honest about how confusing being a teenager can be.
20: Berserk of Gluttony by Isshiki Ichika (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy action story. Fate Graphite works as a gate guard and is looked down on by everyone, because his only skill, Gluttony, seems useless and leaves him always hungry. Then he discovers that when he defeats someone, his skill lets him devour their power. It suits readers who like underdog heroes and grim, growing-stronger fantasy.
21: Old Boy by Garon Tsuchiya and Nobuaki Minegishi (Dark Horse) is a gripping crime thriller. A man named Goto has spent ten years locked in a small private cell, never told who put him there or why. One day he is suddenly set free, and he sets out to find the person responsible and the reason for his imprisonment. It is moody, tense, and a strong choice for readers who love a slow-burning mystery.
22: The Melancholy of Suzumiya Haruhi-chan by Puyo (Yen Press) is a cheerful gag comedy spin-off of Nagaru Tanigawa's Haruhi Suzumiya novels. Haruhi and the members of the SOS Brigade appear in a cute, chibi style, getting into short, silly misadventures that poke fun at the original series. Kyon is still the long-suffering straight man, and Haruhi is still impossible. It is a fun pick for fans who already know the characters.
23: House of Five Leaves by Natsume Ono (Viz Media) is a quiet historical drama set in Edo-period Japan. Masanosuke Akitsu is a skilled but painfully shy samurai who keeps losing work because of his timid nature. He falls in with Yaichi, a charming man who leads a gang of kidnappers called the Five Leaves, and finds himself drawn to them. It is thoughtful and character-driven, a good fit for readers who like slow, atmospheric stories.
26: Outlanders by Johji Manabe (Dark Horse) is a classic sci-fi action story with a dose of romance. When an alien empire invades Earth, photographer Tetsuya Wakatsuki ends up face to face with its leader, Princess Kahm. To everyone's surprise, the warrior princess decides Tetsuya is the man she wants to marry. It is loud, adventurous, and a fun piece of retro manga for fans of space opera.
27: Bloom Into You by Nio Nakatani (Seven Seas) is a thoughtful yuri romance. Yuu Koito has always loved romance stories, but she has never felt the way the characters do. Then she meets Touko Nanami, the admired student council member, who has never been moved by anyone either, until she meets Yuu. It is tender and honest about figuring out your feelings, a good pick for readers who like quiet, emotional love stories.
28: Blue Flag by KAITO (Viz Media) is a heartfelt high school romance and drama. Taichi Ichinose is surprised when Futaba Kuze, a shy girl he barely knows, asks for his help. She has a crush on his best friend, Toma, and she wants Taichi to help her get closer to him. As the three spend more time together, things get complicated in ways none of them expected. It is a thoughtful read for fans of realistic teen drama.
29: Immortal Rain by Kaori Ozaki (Tokyopop) is a moody action fantasy. Rain is a man who cannot die, and there is a huge bounty on his head for anyone who can manage to kill him. Machika, the granddaughter of a legendary bounty hunter, sets out after him, but finds that Rain is not who she expected. It is atmospheric and bittersweet, a good fit for readers who like quiet, sad-eyed heroes.
30: The Vision of Escaflowne by Katsu Aki (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure based on the anime series. Hitomi Kanzaki is an ordinary high school girl until she is pulled into Gaea, a strange world where Earth hangs in the sky. There she meets Van, a young king, and becomes caught up in a war fought with giant armored machines. It blends magic, mecha, and romance, a nice find for fans of the classic show.
31: The Weakest Tamer Began a Journey to Pick Up Trash by Tou Fukino (Seven Seas) is a gentle fantasy adventure. Ivy is a young girl whose tamer skill is rated the weakest possible, so weak that her own village treats her as a burden. She runs away to survive on her own and soon befriends a small, unusual slime. It is cozy and kind-hearted, a nice pick for readers who like slow-paced journeys and found family.
34: The World's Finest Assassin Gets Reincarnated in Another World as an Aristocrat by Rui Tsukiyo (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. The world's best assassin is killed by the organization he served, then offered a second chance by a goddess. He is reborn as Lugh Tuatha Dé, the son of a noble family of assassins, with one task: kill the hero who is fated to destroy the world. It suits readers who like clever, calculating heroes.
37: Cat + Gamer by Wataru Nadatani (Dark Horse) is a cozy slice-of-life comedy. Riko Kozakura is a quiet office worker who spends her free time playing video games. When she takes in a cat, she approaches the whole thing like a new game, figuring out how to keep her new companion happy. It is calm and funny, a sweet pick for cat lovers and gamers alike.
38: Those Who Hunt Elves by Yu Yagami (ADV) is a fantasy comedy with a silly streak. Three people from modern Japan, an actor, an actress, and a military fan, are pulled into a fantasy world along with a tank. The spell that can send them home has been scattered across the bodies of elves, so they have to find the right elves and get a look at their skin. It is goofy road-trip fun for fans of '90s comedy.
40: Cells at Work! Code Black by Shigemitsu Harada (Kodansha) is a darker, funnier spin on the body-as-a-workplace idea. A red blood cell starts his job inside a body that smokes, drinks, and is stressed out, so every shift is a struggle. He and his fellow cells keep working, even as things seem to get worse around them. It is a clever read for adults who like dark comedy with some real science mixed in.
41: Togari by Yoshinori Natsume (Viz Media) is a supernatural action story about a chance at redemption. Tobei is a violent criminal who has ended up in hell after his death. He is offered a deal: armed with a wooden sword called Togari, he must return to the world and destroy 108 sins in 108 days. It is a fast, gritty read for fans of dark action stories.
42: Tokyo Babylon by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a supernatural drama set in 1990s Tokyo. Subaru Sumeragi is a gentle young man who is also the head of a powerful family of spiritual mediums, solving supernatural cases around the city. He is joined by his lively twin sister Hokuto and Seishiro, a friendly veterinarian who claims to be in love with him. It is stylish and moody, a great pick for CLAMP fans.
43: Pluto: Urasawa x Tezuka by Naoki Urasawa (Viz Media) is a sci-fi mystery that retells a classic Astro Boy story. In a world where robots live alongside humans, Europol detective Gesicht, himself a robot, is investigating a string of murders. The victims are some of the most advanced robots in the world, and Gesicht realizes he may be a target too. It is thoughtful and gripping, a strong choice for readers who like crime thrillers.
45: Kaiju Girl Caramelise by Spica Aoki (Yen Press) is a lighthearted romantic comedy. Kuroe Akaishi is a shy, awkward high school girl who keeps a big secret: when her emotions run high, she turns into a giant monster. That makes things very difficult when she starts falling for Arata Minami, the most popular boy in class. It is sweet, silly fun for readers who like quirky shojo.
46: True Beauty by Yaongyi (Webtoon) is a romantic comedy from Korea. Jugyeong Lim has been teased about her looks for years, so she teaches herself to do makeup and transforms her appearance before starting at a new school. Now she is one of the most popular girls around, but she is terrified of anyone seeing her bare face. It is funny, sweet, and a nice fit for fans of school romance.
47: Kamichama Karin by Koge-Donbo (Tokyopop) is a cute magical-girl comedy. Karin Hanazono is a clumsy, unlucky girl, and her beloved cat has just died. When she receives a ring that once belonged to her late mother, she finds out it can turn her into a goddess. Karin quickly gets pulled into a world of magic and rivals. It is a bright, bouncy read for fans of classic shojo.
48: Kamikaze Kaito Jeanne by Arina Tanemura (CMX) is a magical-girl romance. Maron Kusakabe seems like an ordinary high school girl, but she is secretly the phantom thief Jeanne, the reincarnation of Joan of Arc. Her targets are paintings where demons hide, and she steals them to seal the demons away. Meanwhile, a rival thief and a new neighbor keep complicating things. It is a sparkly, heartfelt pick for fans of classic shojo.
49: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion by Majiko! (Bandai) is a sci-fi action manga based on the anime. Lelouch Lamperouge is an exiled prince living in a Japan conquered by the Britannian Empire. When a mysterious girl gives him the power of Geass, letting him command anyone to obey him, he sets out to bring down the empire himself. It is a quick, dramatic read for fans of the show.
50: Cross Game by Mitsuru Adachi (Viz Media) is a baseball story about growing up, family, and first love. Ko Kitamura is the son of a sporting goods shop owner, and he has grown up alongside the four Tsukishima sisters next door, whose family runs a batting center. Their lives are tangled together through childhood, school, and the game of baseball. It is quiet, funny, and very moving, a great pick even for readers who do not follow sports.
52: Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken! by Sumito Oowara (Dark Horse) is a creative comedy about making anime. Midori Asakusa is full of wild ideas, Tsubame Mizusaki loves to animate, and Sayaka Kanamori knows how to make money. Together, the three start their own animation club at school and get to work bringing their imaginations to life. It is a joyful read for anyone who loves art, storytelling, or creative work.
53: Unnamed Memory by Kuji Furumiya (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance. Prince Oscar has been cursed so that no woman can bear his child, putting his royal line at risk. He travels to the tower of Tinasha, the Witch of the Azure Moon, hoping she can break it, and asks her to marry him instead. She refuses, but agrees to stay with him for a year. It is a lovely pick for readers who like romance between two strong-willed leads.
56: Kingdom Hearts by Shiro Amano (Tokyopop) is a family-friendly adventure based on the video game. Sora, Riku, and Kairi live on the peaceful Destiny Islands, until a dark force swallows their home and scatters them. Sora wakes up in a new world holding a mysterious Keyblade and joins Donald Duck and Goofy on a journey to find his friends. It is a fun read for younger fans of Disney and the games.
57: King's Proposal by Koushi Tachibana (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. Mushiki Kuga is a boy who is killed, and the world's strongest witch, Saika Kuozaki, is also fatally wounded. To save them both, the two are merged, and Mushiki finds himself living as Saika while trying to protect her secret. It is a quick, playful read for fans of magic school stories.
60: Demon Diary by Lee Chi Hyong and Kara (Tokyopop) is a fantasy comedy from Korea. Raenef is a new demon lord, but he is far too kind and gentle to act the part. His tutor, Eclipse, is a powerful demon determined to teach him how to be truly evil. Their lessons do not go well, and before long a stubborn young priest gets involved too. It is lighthearted and charming, a nice pick for fans of classic fantasy.
61: Wonder Cat Kyuu-chan by Sasami Nitori (Seven Seas) is a cozy, low-key comedy. A man who lives alone takes in a little cat named Kyuu-chan, and life starts to revolve around his new friend. The two settle into a happy rhythm of play, naps, and snacks. It is gentle and short, a sweet read for cat lovers or anyone who needs a calm, smiling break.
63: Samurai Harem: Asu no Yoichi by Yuu Minamoto (Tokyopop) is a romantic comedy. Yoichi Karasuma was raised in the mountains as a samurai, and he has just arrived in the city to train at a dojo. The dojo belongs to four sisters, and they are not quite sure what to make of a young man who acts like he is from another century. It is silly, light, and a nice pick for fans of harem comedy.
64: Dinosaur Sanctuary by Itaru Kinoshita (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi drama set in a world where dinosaurs never went extinct. Suzuka Suma has just started her dream job as a keeper at Enoshima Dinosaur Land. The park is facing hard times, and she has a lot to learn about caring for the animals. It is thoughtful, with real dinosaur science, a great pick for readers who love animals and workplace stories.
66: Scum's Wish by Mengo Yokoyari (Yen Press) is a mature romance and drama. High school students Hanabi and Mugi look like the perfect couple, but each is secretly in love with someone else, two of their teachers. They agree to date as stand-ins for the people they cannot have. It is raw and emotional, best for older readers who like stories about messy, complicated feelings.
67: Seiho Boys' High School! by Kaneyoshi Izumi (Viz Media) is a school comedy and romance. The students at Seiho are stuck at an all-boys school out in the countryside, and most of them would do almost anything to meet a girl. Each one deals with crushes, friendships, and all the awkwardness of being a teenager. It is funny and good-natured, a fun pick for readers who like ensemble comedies.
72: Mahoromatic by Bow Ditama (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi comedy with a bittersweet streak. Mahoro was once a powerful combat android, but now that she has retired, she has chosen to spend her final days as a maid. She goes to work for Suguru Misato, an orphaned boy who lives alone, and the two quickly become part of each other's lives. It mixes goofy comedy with real tenderness, a good pick for fans of classic anime-era manga.
75: Megatokyo by Fred Gallagher (Dark Horse) is a comedy and romance based on the long-running webcomic. Piro and Largo are two American gamers who take a trip to Tokyo, run out of money, and find themselves stranded there. Piro, a shy artist, gets a job at a manga store, while Largo throws himself at every strange situation. It is funny and heartfelt, a fun pick for readers who love otaku culture.
76: Merman in My Tub by Itokichi (Seven Seas) is a laid-back comedy. Tatsumi is an ordinary young man who comes home to find a merman named Wakasa living in his bathtub. Wakasa is demanding, dramatic, and a big fan of video games, and Tatsumi has no idea what to do with him. It is quick, silly fun for readers who like odd-couple comedies.
77: Failure Frame by Kaoru Shinozaki (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy action story. Touka Mimori is summoned to another world with his entire class, but he is given the lowest possible rank. The goddess who summoned them throws him into a deadly ruin to die. There, Touka discovers his skills are far more dangerous than anyone thought, and he sets out for revenge. It suits readers who like grim, revenge-driven fantasy.
78: First Love Monster by Akira Hiyoshimaru (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy with a strange twist. Kaho Nikaido moves out on her own for high school, and when Kanade Takahashi saves her from an accident, she falls for him on the spot. Kanade is tall and handsome, so it is a shock when she finds out he is actually in fifth grade. It is very silly, and it suits readers who like their comedy over the top.
79: Shonen Note: Boy Soprano by Yuhki Kamatani (Kodansha) is a gentle, quiet drama. Yutaka Aoi is a middle school boy with a beautiful soprano voice who sings in a local choir. He knows his voice will soon change, and he wants to make the most of the time he has left. It is a tender, thoughtful read for anyone who loves music or coming-of-age stories.
80: Silent Möbius by Kia Asamiya (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action series set in a dark future Tokyo. In 2028, the city is under attack from the Lucifer Hawks, creatures from another dimension. A special police unit of women with magical and psychic skills, the AMP, is the only thing standing in their way. It is stylish and atmospheric, a great pick for fans of '90s cyberpunk.
81: Roll Over and Die by Kiki (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy drama. Flum Apricot is chosen to join the hero's party, but her stats are all zero and no one sees the point of her. One member of the party secretly sells her into slavery, and Flum is left to fight for her own life. It is grim and intense, best for older readers who like underdog stories with dark themes.
82: I Kept Pressing the 100-Million-Year Button and Came Out on Top by Syuichi Tsukishima (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. Allen Rodol is a struggling student at a swordsmanship academy with no talent at all. A strange man offers him a button that sends him to a dimension where he must spend 100 million years alone. With nothing else to do, Allen spends that time practicing his sword. It is a fun pick for fans of training-arc fantasy.
84: In the Land of Leadale by Ceez (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy. After years in a hospital bed, Keina Kagami's life support fails, and she wakes up as Cayna, her character from a fantasy game she loved. She discovers the world has moved on 200 years since she last played. It is calm and easygoing, perfect for readers who like slow-paced, slice-of-life isekai.
85: My Friend's Little Sister Has It in for Me! by Mikawaghost (J-Novel Club) is a romantic comedy. Akiteru Oboshi is a practical high school boy who believes romance is a waste of time. That is hard to stick to when his best friend's little sister, Iroha, keeps showing up at his apartment to annoy him. She is cheerful and endlessly teasing, but only around him. It is a fun pick for fans of banter-heavy romance.
87: 7th Time Loop by Minato P (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romance. Rishe has lived her life six times, each time ending in her death at age 20, and she has picked up a lot of skills along the way. On her seventh loop, she meets Arnold Hein, the prince who killed her in a past life, and he asks her to marry him. It is clever and charming, a good pick for fans of villainess stories.
88: Monster Girl Doctor by Yoshino Origuchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Glenn Litbeit is a doctor who runs a clinic in a town where humans and monsters live side by side. With his assistant Sapphee, a lamia, he treats a wide range of monster girls with all sorts of unusual problems. It is light and good-natured, a fun pick for fans of creature-filled fantasy.
90: The World's Finest Assassin Gets Reincarnated in Another World as an Aristocrat by Rui Tsukiyo (Viz Media) is a fantasy action story. The world's best assassin is killed by the organization he served, then offered a second chance by a goddess. He is reborn as Lugh Tuatha Dé, the son of a noble family of assassins, with one task: kill the hero who is fated to destroy the world. It suits readers who like clever, calculating heroes.
91: Slayers by Hajime Kanzaka (CPM) is a fantasy comedy and adventure. Lina Inverse is a teenage sorceress with a big appetite, a short temper, and enough magic to flatten a town. Along with swordsman Gourry Gabriev, she wanders from place to place, looking for treasure and trouble. It is a fun, fast read for fans of classic '90s fantasy.
93: Bofuri: I Don't Want to Get Hurt, So I'll Max Out My Defense by Jirou Oimoto (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Kaede Honjo is new to virtual reality games, and since she hates getting hurt, she puts all her points into defense. Playing as Maple, she turns out to be almost impossible to damage, and she keeps finding strange new skills. It is light, cheerful fun for fans of game stories.
94: Phantom of the Idol by Hijiki Isoflavone (Kodansha) is a supernatural comedy. Yuya Niyodo is a member of the idol group ZINGS, but he has no energy for the job. Then the ghost of a young idol, Asahi Mogami, starts possessing him on stage, and suddenly his performances are amazing. It is a funny, upbeat pick for fans of idol stories.
95: Heaven's Design Team by Hebi-Zou and Tsuta Suzuki (Kodansha) is a workplace comedy with a clever premise. God has decided to create animals for Earth, but has handed the job to a team of designers. Kimura is the new go-between, passing God's requests on to the team and watching them come up with the creatures. It is gentle and funny, with lots of real animal facts.
96: Magus of the Library by Mitsu Izumi (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure about the love of books. Theo is a poor boy in a small town who is teased for his appearance but loves to read. When he meets a group of kafna, the librarians who protect the great library, he sets his heart on becoming one of them. It is beautifully drawn and a great pick for readers who love books about books.
97: Lucky Star by Kagami Yoshimizu (Bandai) is a laid-back slice-of-life comedy. Konata Izumi is a high school girl who loves anime, manga, and video games far more than studying. She spends her days chatting with her friends, the twins Kagami and Tsukasa and the polite, brainy Miyuki, about snacks, homework, and the little puzzles of everyday life. It is short, low-key fun, a great fit for fans of otaku humor and cozy school comedies.
98: Strobe Edge by Io Sakisaka (Viz Media) is a sweet high school romance and drama. Ninako Kinoshita has never been in love, but everything changes when she gets to know Ren Ichinose, the boy every girl at school is crazy about. Ninako falls for him, but she knows he is already seeing someone else. It is honest and tender, a great pick for fans of classic shojo romance.
99: Saekano: How to Raise a Boring Girlfriend by Fumiaki Maruto (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy. Tomoya Aki is an otaku who wants to make his own dating-sim game. When he meets Megumi Kato, a quiet, plain girl, he decides she will be his heroine. He sets out to build a team of creators, which pulls in a few girls from his past. It is a fun pick for fans of otaku comedy.
